Computer simulation results carried out to investigate the comparative performance of the algorithm and of MUSIC under various conditions are included. The algorithm has superior performance to the MUSIC algorithm and usually converges in a few steps.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A maximum entropy solution for the undetermined electromagnetic field within a volume
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The Gibbs maximum entropy (GME) solution is presented for the problem of estimating the sinusoidal electric field within a given volume of subject to constraints of measured electric field at I/sub 1/ points and zero tangential electric field at I/sub 2/ points. The field is expanded in a set of K solenoidal and perhaps irrotational (curl=0) modes with unknown amplitudes, defined within a convenient volume. Since the number of complex data in the three spatial directions, 3(I/sub 1/+I/sub 2/), is presumed to be considerably less than the number of complex amplitudes K, this is an undetermined problem.

articleTitle: Spectral representation of the Green's functions for microstrip antennas on cylindrical substrates
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: It is well-known that the angular Fourier series is poorly convergent in a numerical implementation of the Green's functions, especially for electrically large patches and cylinders. Using the theory of characteristic Green's functions, the author represents the components of the Green's dyad as spectral integrals over a continuum of angular and axial wavenumbers, thereby obviating the need for Fourier series. The angular periodicity that is intrinsic to an electric dipole located on a cylindrical microstrip substrate can be recovered from the spectral integrals by applying completeness relations for the angular-domain characteristic Green's function.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Rough surface scattering. I. Electromagnetic scattering and shadowing from an exponentially distributed rough surface
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: For the purposes of rough surface scattering analysis it is often desirable to model the rough surface by a joint probability density function (JPDF). To date a considerable amount of work in this area has been done using a Gaussian and an exponential-type JPDF. Unlike the Gaussian JPDF, the exponential-type JPDF fails to meet the requirement that the random variables (which represent surface heights) become independent when uncorrelated. An exponential JPDF which splits into the product two sided exponential PDFs has been derived by applying certain nonlinear transformation to the square of the envelope and the phase of a narrowband Gaussian random process. The application of this JPDF is presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Study on multilayer microstrip antenna
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A method has been devised to analyze a multilayer electrically thick microstrip antenna excited by a probe. The authors derive the field expression of a horizontal electric dipole located in multilayer media. Assuming the current on the feeding probe is uniform, an integral equation for the patch current is derived. The impedance is obtained using Galerkin's method. The EMF method is used to obtain the antenna impedance. This method is illustrated by the analysis of a microstrip antenna with an air gap, but can be used to analyze any multilayer microstrip antenna. This method was verified experimentally.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Feedback formulation for multiple scatterers
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A numerical method for the scattering problem is presented that uses feedback formulation to model multiple interactions between objects, expressing incidents and scattered fields as sums of cylindrical modes, resulting in smaller matrix sizes. The method entails three steps: the characterization of each object, then the transformation of each emerging mode from one object into incident fields on the others and then the computation of the scattered fields.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Electromagnetic transient response of rotationally symmetric permeable conducting objects
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Low-frequency transient response is often used to detect or identify buried objects. At sufficiently low frequencies, the signal penetration in the ground is high and the air-earth interface has a negligible effect on the return response. The use of an exciting current loop also minimizes the ground conductivity effect. These properties are used to develop an efficient numerical method to compute and study the transient response of permeable objects. A few representative results for rotationally symmetric objects are presented and discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A fundamental source of error in the scattering method of measuring antenna surface field distributions
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: An analysis of the measurement of a general standing wave distribution on a transmission line using a modulated scattering probe is presented. This is classified as a measurement in a reactive-field region of a normal-mode of a closed system. Details of theory and validation are discussed and a source of possible error is revealed when it is applied to antennas. In those cases where the forward scattered signal is not reflected back to the measuring system, the law relating the field to the measurable quantity may range from a square law to a fourth-power relationship. Thus, depending on conditions at the detector and whether scattering is occurring on a transmission-line-type structure or not, the measured quantity may be related to the surface field through a power law of index anywhere between 2 and 6. For travelling wave antennas, the distribution that is obtained is not necessarily that which is exclusively associated with the nonradiating surface wave, but it includes components near the ends that contribute to the radiation from the structure.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A direct look at creeping waves
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: To the human eye light rays appear as entities emanating from well defined bright regions on a scattering body. It is argued that these regions, whether associated with specular reflection, edge diffraction, or creeping waves (appearing as bright boundaries on curved bodies), can each be observed and studied independently using the filtering functions inherent in vision. The author discusses processing of a similar kind, emulated computationally, by simple windowing, of computed radiation. Sample data are shown that were obtained by applying to the outgoing axial field component a fourth-order Blackman-Harris window that is centered 90 degrees behind the observer and extends over 180 degrees . The magnitude (in terms of a scattering width) of the windowed radiation from an impedance cylinder is graphed for various impedance levels. Remapping these results provides the decay and launching constants for the dominant creeping wave modes.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Mutual coupling between two slots on a circular cylinder
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: An expression for mutual reaction between two arbitrarily located slots on an infinitely long conducting cylinder is derived. This stationary expression is used to obtain a formula for mutual admittance and coupling coefficient. The numerical results are presented and discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A triplate stripline slot antenna developed for time-domain measurements on phased arrays
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A frequency-independent, triplate feed structure is described that is easily matched, even if slot shape and dimensions are varied, and has the advantage of causing a minimum of disturbance to the aperture fields. This feed structure does not extend the impulse response of the antenna. The properties of the slots can thus be separated from the effects of the edges of the ground plane by making measurements in the time domain. The results show that the resonant frequency may be predicted by simple cavity theory.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Radar: from Hertz to the 21st century
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Summary form only given. A review is presented of the major radar applications and the technologies that led to these applications. The significance of radar for civil air-traffic control and military air defense is emphasized. Also discussed is the direction indicated for high-power radar transmitters, large antennas, waveform design, signal processing, data processing, and sensor integration. Mention is made of the basic information available from the radar echo signal and its utility for remote sensing and target recognition, the potential for wide-area surveillance from space, and the capabilities and applications of radar operating outside the usual microwave frequency band.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Polarization efficiency statistics
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The mean and RMS (root-mean-square) statistics of the polarization efficiency between an incident wave and a receiving antenna are derived. The mean polarization efficiency equals or exceeds one-half when the handedness of the incident field and receiving antenna is similar and is less than or equal to one-half when the handedness is dissimilar. The standard deviation of the polarization efficiency has a significantly higher value than that anticipated from Gaussian statistics. These statistics provide estimates for the sensitivity loss in system operation and provide values for polarization mismatch loss needed in error budget projections of measurement accuracy or RF system performance.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: SEM poles of spheroids
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The ray method is used to calculate the SEM (singularity expansion method) poles of spheroids based on the concept of orthogonal decomposition. As an example, the calculated results are used to verify the correctness of the computing model, which extends the ray method for calculating SEM poles from two-dimensional scatterers to three-dimensional ones.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Radiation and scattering by infinite microstrip patch arrays on anisotropic substrates
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: An analysis is presented of an infinite array of printed patches on a grounded anisotropic-dielectric slab. The array is considered as both a transmitter fed by idealized probes and as a scatterer of plane waves. For the transmitter case, the input reflection coefficient versus incident angle is computed for various loads and substrates. The theory in both cases is confirmed by comparing its limit to isotropic cases with previous analyses. The inputs to the analysis are the substrate parameters, the array grid geometry, the patch dimensions including probe position, and the probe load impedance, which is assumed conjugate matched at broadside for the transmit case.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Dielectric-covered waveguide longitudinal slots
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The presence of a dielectric substrate can alter the characteristics of the individual slots and considerably affect the mutual coupling. To analyze or design such an array, a procedure that includes the above effects is presented. It is based on work by R.S. Elliott et al. (1984) on the analysis and design of similar arrays without the dielectric cover. The authors show how the method is used to study the effect of the cover on the slots' resonant length, resonant admittance, and mutual coupling.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Effect of a finite ground plane thickness on the radiation pattern of an aperture antenna
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A convenient procedure to obtain the radiation pattern of slot antennas consists of assuming that the conducting ground plane containing the slot is infinitely long. While this may be adequate for obtaining the radiation pattern in the half space of the aperture, for obtaining the complete radiation pattern of the antenna the proper dimensions of the ground plane have to be considered. The effect of the ground plane thickness on the radiation pattern for aperture antennas with the slots assumed as sources of cylindrical or spherical waves is examined using the geometrical theory of diffraction (GTD). The diffraction from the upper and lower edges of the ground plane was calculated considering the multiple diffractions between the edges. Numerical results are presented and discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Discretizing technique for a rectangular grid array with arbitrary shape aperture
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The excitation of discrete planar arrays with circular boundaries is often determined by conventional sampling of the continuous aperture distributions. If the number of elements is large, so that the sampling interval is small, this can be a satisfactory procedure so long as some pattern degradation is acceptable. A discretizing process using a perturbation technique due to R.S. Elliot (1981) is extended. The modified technique uses a contour map to describe sidelobe peak topography and the sidelobe topography is used to effect pattern improvement. Many points, instead of a single point, are sampled in the vicinity of each lobe for weighting purposes. A gradual change (towards the desired pattern) algorithm is then introduced to maintain pattern stability. The technique was applied to a 140-element aperture (35 elements per quadrant) to obtain 3-dB Chebyshev-like sidelobes. After the iterations, most of the sidelobes were between 30 and 32 dB.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A comparison of some radiation boundary conditions for differential equation calculations of scattering
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: An approximate boundary condition is necessary to close the computational grid for a differential-equation-based solution (either in the frequency or time domain) of an electromagnetic scattering problem. While the asymptotic form for r to infinity is well-known, it is not sufficient for large problems. For efficiency, one needs to find higher-order boundary conditions that allow the computational grid to be terminated as close to the scatterer as possible. The author discusses the two-dimensional, frequency-domain case in detail. However, the results for three dimensions and/or the time domain are quite similar.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An exploration of the capability of the hybrid finite element method for EM scattering by inhomogeneous cylinders
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The authors present a formulation which avoids the partly full and partly sparse nonsymmetric matrix by modifying the coupling technique. It allows one to make full use of the nice property of the coefficient matrix. This further enhances the computational efficiency and expands the capability of the hybrid finite-element method (HFEM). It is concluded that HFEM is currently one of the most efficient numerical techniques for study of two-dimensional scattering problems involving inhomogeneous dielectric and/or magnetic media.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: MUSIC algorithm in a scattering environment
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A method of spatial filtering is proposed as a preprocessor to restore the high-resolution performance of the MUSIC algorithm when used with a linear array for angle of arrival estimation in a scattering environment. The method is based on the assumption that plane-wave arrivals and their scatterings are well separated in spatial frequency (in angle). Simulation results are shown for the case of scattering from an infinite circular cylinder, using discrete prolate spheroidal sequences as the optimum bandpass preprocessing filters, and a uniformly spaced linear array.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Experimental evidence that microstrip patches and flat dipoles on grounded substrates are the same type of element
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Microstrip patches and flat dipoles on grounded substrates are shown to be special cases of a more general type of radiating element whose design may be modeled by a suitable combination of electric and magnetic current sources that themselves are a function of geometrical dimensions, especially the substrate thickness. Extension of the inner conductor of a coaxial line can be used to feed resonant half-wave dipoles one-quarter wavelength in front of a ground plane without the structure becoming effectively a top-loaded monopole. Though novel and unconventional, the feed has mechanical simplicity and warrants more detailed study. No reactive network is needed for wideband impedance matching of elements irrespective of substrate thickness provided the geometry of the patch and the feed point connection are chosen properly.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Optimum coaxial cavity horn for high aperture efficiency and low cross-polarization
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A coaxial cavity-feed horn has been analyzed using the geometrical theory of diffraction, and the radiation characteristics are investigated numerically. Surface integral equations are formulated, and the moment method is used to reduce the integral equation to a matrix equation. The copolar and cross-polar radiation patterns, as well as the aperture efficiency and phase center location, are computed. Good agreement between the computed and measured data is observed with very good symmetry between E- and H-plane patterns. This process results in a feed with a cross polarization level of -28.77 dB. It is believed that the high cross polarization level originally observed is due to the separation of the phase centers of the circular waveguide and the coaxial cavity, which caused a large separation between the phase center location of the E- and H-planes. Thus, the coaxial cavity depth has been modified to correct the phase center, and the coaxial cavity wall has been extended beyond the circular waveguide aperture to correct the H-plane amplitude pattern.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Optimum localization of coherent signals having diverse polarizations
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The problem of estimating the angles of arrival (AOA) of narrowband sources, having the same frequency, is considered. The authors previously derived (1986) a computationally attractive method for computing the maximum-likelihood (ML) estimator for the case of an identically polarized array. The method is based on an iterative technique referred to as alternating projection maximization (APM), which transforms the multivariate nonlinear maximization problem into a sequence of much simpler one-dimensional maximizations. Here, the ML estimator and the APM algorithm are derived for an array of antennas having diverse polarizations. Since the algorithm realizes the ML estimator, it is applicable equally well for signals that are either uncorrelated or fully correlated. The results from two simulations are reviewed to demonstrate the performance of the ML estimator for the diverse polarization array case.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Peak sidelobe of phase weighted array antennas
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Y.C. Guo and M.S. Smith (IEE Proc-H, vol.130, no.5 (1983)) described a technique for peak sidelobe reduction in a linear phased array called phase weighting. With this technique, the theory of stochastic processes is used to predict the sidelobe levels achievable using phase weighting. Y.C. Guo and M.S. Smith used a simplified formula to make predictions, which could then be compared with empirical results. They found good agreement in some cases, but not when the first sidelobe level was comparable with the peak random sidelobe. Here, an improved prediction formula is used, which accounts for the first sidelobe's effects and shows good agreement with the empirical results in all cases. Comparison between predictions and empirical results from computer simulation show good agreement.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A parasitic stacked patch antenna element for use in a 44 GHz MMIC phased array
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The current 44 GHz MMIC (monolithic microwave integrated-circuit) antenna arrays, with active devices located on the same substrate as the radiating elements, typically require GaAs substrate thicknesses of about 5 mils for optimal active component performance. This substrate thickness would severely restrict the bandwidth of conventional microstrip antennas. This problem has been largely overcome by using a stacked patch antenna element, which can yield bandwidths of greater than 20% in some cases. Using a 10.5 dielectric-constant material for the lower substrate, six waveguide simulators were used to measure the active impedance of the scaled 44 GHz stacked patch antenna element as a function of (1) the dielectric constant of the cover material, (2) the air gap spacing between the lower and upper substrates, and (3) the radius of the cover patch. The voltage-standing-wave ratios (VSWRs) for the stacked patch element for each scan condition as a function of the dielectric cover parameters are given in a table. The air-gap spacing and upper patch radius were empirically determined so that the VSWRs for each scan condition were mutually minimized. In this manner the VSWR was held relatively constant across the measured scan range of the array.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Exact image analysis of three-layer microstrip structure
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A three-layer microstrip structure is analyzed using the exact image method. From the Fourier domain reflection coefficient an asymptotic term and the surface wave poles are extracted, and the remaining function is expanded into a sum of pole terms (Mittag-Leffler expansion). Hence the inverse Laplace transform of the coefficient can be presented simply as a well converging series of exponential functions. As an example, it is shown how the method is applicable to shielded microstrip structures. The detailed image functions are shown for a microstrip antenna above a two-layer biological medium, using as the three layers, substrate, skin, and fat.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A study of two-dimensional cylinders illuminated by TE polarized microwaves using the k-space algorithm
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: One comparison of the numerical modeling techniques applied to the absorption of electromagnetic energy by organic tissues is that of D.T. Borup et al. (IEEE Transaction and Microwave Theory and Techniques, vol.T-MTT-35, p.383-395, 1987) that compared the fast Fourier transform-conjugate-gradient method (FFT-CGM) with the finite-element-time-domain methods. The authors expand and elaborate the findings of Borup et al. (BSG) for the case of TE-polarized illumination. The solution technique in this comparison, which is referred as the k-space algorithm, differs in (at least) two ways from the FFT-CGM employed in the BSG study. First, all of the integrals arising from the application of the method of moments formalism are transformed to line integrals along the cell boundaries. Seconds, the system of linear equations arising from the application of the method of moments is solved by iterated minimization of the squared error using several variational functions. Considering TE polarization of the illuminating plane wave, the effect of increasing the number of points in the mesh on the convergence of the solution is presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Microstrip patch phased array on a cylinder
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The radiation behavior of patch elements in a phase steered array has been documented. The frequency of operation was set to 5.7 GHz. Beam steering +or-30 degrees in the azimuth without phase compensation to the outermost elements was specified. Beam steering in the elevation plane was also desirable as an option, as well as circular polarization. The patch element was theoretically described by surface currents on the substrate, using two current modes, and one axial and one circumferential. The mutual coupling was incorporated by adopting an element by element procedure. The scattering matrix as measured from a center element was implemented. The return loss measured at each element with the surrounding elements terminated in matched loads was overall better than 20 dB at the center frequency. The measured active element pattern for the center element showed good agreement with the calculated radiation pattern with the mutual coupling included.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: OSRC method for acoustic scattering and electromagnetic scattering by dielectric cylinders
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A special system of orthogonal coordinates for which the surface of an arbitrary three-dimensional scatterer locally coincides with a constant coordinate surface can be used to factor the scalar three-dimensional Helmholtz equation to get a one-way differential equation. Such a one-way operator is used in the on surface radiation condition (OSRC) method. This has been applied to three-dimensional scalar scattering by acoustically soft and hard scatterers and two-dimensional electromagnetic scattering by metallic cylinders. These results are extended to acoustic scattering by general acoustic scatterers and electromagnetic scattering by dielectric cylinders.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Measurement of diffraction from isolation edges
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The use of collimated radiation in the near field to produce windowed illumination of test objects is demonstrated to be useful for obtaining experimental data from relatively isolated edges. This is accomplishing by illuminating only about one-third of the edge with a lens-collimated horn antenna. These measurements can be calibrated to yield absolute values for the edge diffraction coefficients for comparison with calculated predictions. The results is experimental data that are in excellent agreement with calculated data.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On transmission characteristics of an infinite plane grating embedded in a dielectric slab (TM-case)
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The author analyzes the quasi-two-dimensional problem rigorously, where the incident angle is oblique to X-axis of the wire grating, the polarization is TM to Z-direction, and the grating is embedded in the dielectric slab. The analytical method used is the magnetic vector potential (two-components) method for an equivalent magnetic walled H-waveguide with spacing equal to the wire grating period. The analysis can be used to design multilayer gratings using the network cascade method.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Solutions of Maxwell equations by matrix formulation
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Formulas are developed for directly finding electromagnetic field wherein the vector differential operations are replaced by simple vector algebraic operations. The resulting field solutions are exact, with no approximation used, and can be explicitly written in a matrix formulation such that both the current distribution and the resulting field are conveniently expressed in terms of various coordinate systems. If the radiating fields in the near- or far-field are of primary interest, the formulation is greatly simplified; the electric and magnetic fields are simply determined by matrix product whenever the radiation vector is calculated.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Electromagnetic imaging of complex permittivity profiles by moment method in the spectral domain
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A novel inverse scheme applicable in the spectral domain is suggested to find a proper way to remedy the ill-posedness inherent to inverse scattering problems. A cylindrical object with complex relative dielectric constant in arbitrary cross section S is treated. Numerical simulation results are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The effect of wavenumber filtering on synthetic two-dimensional magnetotelluric data
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The magnetotelluric (MT) method, an electromagnetic sounding technique used in geophysical exploration, is considered. The MT method is based upon the measurement of the naturally occurring electromagnetic field at the surface of the Earth and the interpretation of the surface electromagnetic field to infer subsurface structure. When the region of the Earth being surveyed by the MT method has strong lateral heterogeneities, information about the deep structure of the Earth is obscured by near surface features, leading to significant interpretational problems. A low-pass wavenumber filtering method used to deal with this problem is described and evaluated by comparing the calculated apparent resistivity of a model of the Earth consisting of a two-dimensional heterogeneous layer on the surface of a horizontally stratified Earth with the wavenumber filtered apparent resistivity. Its effectiveness is confirmed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Secondary diffraction of plane waves by a dielectric strip
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The authors derive the scattered fields due to the secondary diffraction of plane waves by a dielectric strip. The strip is simulated by a pair of boundary conditions derived by A.D. Rawlins (1977).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Eigenfunction expansion of the dyadic Green's functions in spherical coordinates
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The dyadic Green's functions (DGFs) in spherical coordinates for free space are determined by the theory of distributions. It is also shown that the electric and the magnetic DGF solutions satisfy the dyadic version of Maxwell's equations and of the equation of current continuity.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Radar imaging with partially coherent array
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A partially coherent array (PCA) is proposed for achieving high angular resolution. This array is considered to have mostly noncoherent channels. With a limitation on the field of view of the imaging array, the missing phases of the noncoherent channels can be reconstructed through an iterative Fourier transformation process. After this process a PCA can perform imaging like a totally coherent array.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Resistive tapers that place nulls in the scattering patterns of strips
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The scattering patterns of a perfectly conducting strip can be modified by making part of the strip from resistive materials. A description is given of a method of deriving a complex resistive taper that places multiple nulls in the bistatic scattering pattern or one null in the backscattering pattern of a strip.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Identification of a target in presence of ground clutter using polarisation
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A polarimetric method of identification of a target in the presence of ground clutter is examined. The clutter is modeled as a two-layer random medium. The complex scattering matrix for the clutter is obtained by using Born approximations carried to the second order to extract the cross-polarized scattered fields. The test target used is a loop of conducting wire oriented arbitrarily. It is found that choice of polarization is one of the key factors if one has to identify targets in the presence of clutter. The author does not take into account the mutual coupling between the target and the cluttering body. The results are analyzed and discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Time domain inverse scattering method for one-dimensional inhomogeneous layered medium
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A discussion is presented of the time-domain inverse scattering problem for the case in which the electric dipole is located above a one-dimensional inhomogeneous layered medium. The inversion algorithm proposed for determining the permittivity and conductivity profiles is not mathematically exact but is simple and practical.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fourier spectra of the near fields from two-dimensional sources or scatterers in uniform motion
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The theory of radiation from two-dimensional harmonic sources in uniform motion is studied. The fields detected by a stationary observer turn out to be rather complicated functions of time which exhibit both amplitude and phase modulation. Attention is focused on the frequency content of such signals. The method applies to sources with constant velocity and is valid for observers located in the near field or in the far field. Numerical results are presented for a moving line source. It is shown how the method can be extended to the spectra of the fields scattered by a two-dimensional moving body. This is illustrated by the case of a moving perfectly conducting circular cylinder immersed in an incident-plane E-wave.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Multiple diffraction among impedance wedges
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A method due to M.I. Herman and I.L. Volakis (IEEE Trans. Ant. and Prop., vol.36, p.664-78, May 1988) is extended to the development of double and triple diffraction coefficients as applied to a pair of impedance wedges. Particular emphasis is given in the evaluation of suitable diffraction coefficients that remain uniform at all reflection and shadow boundaries associated with the multiple wedges. The extended spectral ray method is used along with a more generalized interpretation of the spectral waves.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Incoherent microwave imaging using frequency diversity technique
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The analytical and numerical results of the microwave tomographic image reconstruction of a three-dimensional incoherent source using the frequency diversity technique and the projection-slice theorem are presented. The results demonstrate that a large vector-k-space volume of the far field mutual coherence function can be synthesized by an incoherent microwave imaging system using a frequency diversity technique, and the tomographic image of a 3-D incoherent source can then be reconstructed based on the projection-slice theorem.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: HF broadcast transmitting antennas
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: An overview is presented of high-frequency (HF) broadcast transmitting antennas. For long-range broadcasting, high-power wideband directive antennas with slewing and beam shaping capabilities are needed. The design requirements, state-of-the-art, and the future trend of these antennas are discussed. Also discussed are the power-handling capability of the antenna, its mechanical requirements, and siting conditions. Currently available HF broadcast antennas are examined. It is shown that beam slewing in discrete steps can be achieved by phase adjustments between antenna elements and between antenna stacks. Continuous beam slewing in the horizontal direction is achievable, in principle, by the phased-array approach.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The history of electromagnetics as Hertz would have known it
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Summary form only given. The eighteenth century witnessed a rich series of discoveries of electric and magnetic phenomena. Gray identified the property of electric conduction and the inverse square law of electrostatics was developed by Franklin, Priestley, Robinson, Cavendish, and ultimately Coulomb. Michell showed that the same law applied in magnetostatics and this was reinforced quantitatively by Coulomb. In the nineteenth century, Volta invented the first chemical battery, which permitted Davey and Ampere to develop what would ultimately become Ohm's law. Poisson put the laws of electrostatics and magnetostatics in an elegant mathematical framework. The two disciplines were joined by Oersted's discovery of the action of an electric current on a compass needle. Shortly thereafter Biot and Savart, and independently Ampere, couched this discovery in mathematical terms. Oersted's experiment was enlarged by Faraday, who presented to the world the first electric motor. Faraday later demonstrated the converse of Oersted's experiment, showing that a moving magnetic field could induce an electric current, which he quickly followed with developments of the transformer and the electric generator. Faraday's series of experiments were given their theoretical counterpart by Maxwell, whose equations predicted the existence of as-yet-undetected electromagnetic waves. The culmination of this remarkable train of scientific advances was provided by Hertz, whose experiments validated Maxwells's prediction.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Grating lobe pattern mapping over pitch and roll of a triangular lattice planar array
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A method is presented to determine the maximum lattice spacing of a triangular lattice array that will maintain a clear specified scan area (clear from spurious grating lobe beams) as the antenna proceeds through a specified pitch and roll. A uniformly spaced lattice of isotropic radiators is assumed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Some considerations in remote sensing of rain by polarization diversity radars
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The author investigates the coherency matrix measurement for polarization scanning, with emphasis on propagation effects in precipitation media. An analytical description of propagation effects for partially polarized backscatter, using linear polarization as a basis is developed. A comparison is made with a formulation based on circular polarization. For this comparison, and for verifying the analytical models, consecutive radar polarimetric measurements at scanning linear polarization, on the rainstorm described here and on other forms of precipitation are examined.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Characteristics of the scanning antenna with a plane aperture
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The transient behavior of a rectangular scanning antenna was studied previously (1985) by the author. The analytical method is extended to the scanning antenna with a plane aperture. The author considers the radiation field to be the output of a time-invariant system. This makes it possible to analyze the characteristics of the antenna with linear system theory. He obtains the transfer function to prove that the system is stable and to provide a reliable basis for the transient analysis. The gain of the system can be also obtained. It is shown that the energy ratio of output and input in the scanning direction can be expressed by the gain of the system and the RMS (root-mean-square) bandwidth of the input signal. A simple formula directly calculable in the time domain is found for the far field.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Study of installing TV transmitting antennas of different frequency channels on the same horizontal plane of a transmitting tower
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The radiation characteristics of dipoles near a reflecting cylinder are analyzed, and the possibility of installing TV transmitting antennas of two frequency channels on the same horizontal plane of a transmitting tower is investigated by using a combination of the moment method and the theory of reciprocity. The computational results show that, in general, a circular cross-section of the transmitting tower is a favorable shape to obtain better omnidirectional radiation patterns for different frequency channels. Although only some specific shapes of the cylinder cross-section and channels are considered, the technique is suitable for this type of problem with arbitrary shapes and other channels.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Microstrip-fed ANSERLIN antenna elements and arrays
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Methods of constructing ANSERLIN (annular sector radiating line) antennas using microstrip feedlines are demonstrated. The antennas are well matched at all frequencies where the structural discontinuities are very small in wavelengths. Well-formed circularly polarized beams are obtained over bandwidths exceeding 25%. As much as 60% of the input power can be radiated from a single element. A six-element array has demonstrated the application of microstrip feedlines for series interconnections.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Application of field theory analysis of multiport-multidiscontinuity structures to circular-electric mode waveguide junctions and couplers
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The generalized scattering matrix for a generalized two-port discontinuity is used to analyze a junction between a composite region comprising a coaxial waveguide with a hollow inner conductor and a circular cylindrical waveguide. The combination of the two multiport discontinuities by a circular waveguide section is used to obtain a four-port device termed Marcatili's coupler.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new method of pattern synthesis for linear equal-spaced array
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A method based on the expansions of eigenmodes for the excitation and magnitude patterns and the iterative modification of phase pattern are used successfully. This method is more accurate than the method of N. Inagaki and R.J. Garbacz (1982) and simpler than the method of moments. In addition, this modified eigenmodes method can be extended to synthesizing a linear array of anisotropic (directive) elements.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: New formulations for mutual coupling computations of antennas mounted on Eisenhart coordinate surfaces
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Summary form only given. A uniform approach is proposed for the mutual-coupling analysis of conformal antennas for all the coordinate surfaces of the Eisenhart coordinating systems. Using this approach, along with the uniform theory of diffraction (UTD), several hitherto unsolved quadric surfaces like the general paraboloid of revolution can be conveniently tackled. The general approach consists of parameterizing the coordinate surface of interest in the appropriate coordinate system and carrying out a systematic global analysis, using the properties of differential geometry, to obtain all the geodesic parameters associated with surface-diffracted ray paths.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Minimizing the number of control elements in phased arrays by subarraying
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A set of design curves are presented that can be used to optimize the tradeoff between field of view and subarray size, the subarray size being a function of the number of elements in a subarray and the interelement spacing. In determining these curves, an optimum spacing is determined as a function of n/sub s/, the number of elements along a side. The scan loss is determined as a function of n/sub s/ and the maximum beam scan angle ( theta /sub 0/) only. The reduction in number of phase shifters resulting from using a subarray is also determined as a function of n/sub s/ and theta /sub 0/ only.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Development of EM modeling software performance standards
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The author discusses the issues of how computer models might be characterized and compared, validation of such models by error checking and error analysis, and development of canonical reference solutions and software performance standards. A discussion is presented of the internal and external validation procedures. The types of errors that can render the cross-entropy method (CEM) uncertain are also examined.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The use of reactive loading for dual-band circularly polarized characteristics in microstrip antennas
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A diagonal-fed rectangular microstrip antenna is reactively loaded to produce a dual-band circularly polarized radiator. The impedance locus demonstrates the dual-band behavior of the radiator. The impedances at the two bands are less than the impedance of the unloaded structure. The axial ratio at broadside for each of the bands is about the same as the variation that resulted from the unloaded radiator (about 2 dB). There is an apparent asymmetry in a radiation pattern. This undesirable effect could be due to the method used to load the radiator, in which case it would be reduced somewhat if true monolithic loads were used.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Progress toward a benchmark solution for 3-D, perfectly conducting scatterers with edges and corners
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The authors present the predicted and measured E-plane, H-plane, and 45 degrees -plane scattered fields from the perfectly conducting cube for broadside plane-wave incidence. Although the scattering patterns are obtained for a plane-wave incident broadside upon the front face of the cube, the magnetic-field integral equation solutions can easily accommodate plane-wave illumination from an arbitrary direction, or illumination by an incident field other than a plane wave. However, the uniform high-frequency solution is valid only for broadside plane-wave incidence.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Discontinuities of dielectric loaded waveguides
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Scattering of axially symmetric or hybrid incident modes by discontinuities in the cross section of a dielectric loaded waveguide is determined using the mode-matching technique. Typical numerical examples are presented, showing the convergence of the calculations, the variation of the reflection coefficient of an incident hybrid mode with frequency, and the variation with the structure parameters. Discontinuities in dielectric loaded waveguides are accurately characterized using mode matching. Typical results showing hybrid mode scattering by such discontinuities are presented. Although the example presented is in the C-band, this type of transmission medium can potentially be used for millimeter, submillimeter, and optical wavelengths to reduce the transmission loss.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Analysis of the effect of finite gap width on the admittance of solid circular dipole
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The authors consider a center-fed solid circular cylindrical dipole radiating in a circular waveguide terminated in infinite ground planes. Numerical results show how the input admittance depends on the dipole length, feed gap width, and waveguide radius. From the input admittances of the enclosed system, the oscillations of which exhibit a decaying almost periodic variation as the radius increases, the input admittances of dipoles radiating in free space are estimated by averaging the admittances of the bounded system over two periods for large radius-to-wordlength ratios.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new design procedure for optimum gain pyramidal horns
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A procedure for designing optimum gain pyramidal horns has been developed. It offers exact dimensions with a simple and efficient numerical method, compared to a previous design method using geometrical approximations and a trial-and-error process. The technique has been validated both analytically and experimentally, and should prove useful for microwave antenna designers.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design of an inexpensive multi-mode satellite tracking feed
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A satellite tracking feed system is described in which only the TE/sub 11/ and TM/sub 01/ modes of the circularly polarized signal are used. The tracking feed was designed to operate between 20.2 and 21.2 GHz. The essential component of the feed consists of a conventional smooth circular waveguide, whose diameter is sufficiently large enough to support both modes. It has a rectangular port orthogonal to the circular waveguide, and a resonant ring, acting as a mode filter which separates the modes. The TM/sub 01/ mode is then coupled from the circular waveguide by a coaxial probe, which is matched to a 50 Omega coaxial connector using a tapered transition. The feed is designed to be used with either a corrugated horn or a dual-mode horn.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Coupling between printed dipole and coplanar strip transmission line
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: An analysis is presented of the parasitic coupling between a printed circuit dipole suspended above a coplanar strip transmission line. The dipole is centered over and is perpendicular to the transmission line. This configuration occurs in antenna arrays which use parasitic dipole elements, such as the Barbano log-periodic array. This analysis show that there is significant coupling between a printed dipole and a coplanar strip transmission line, which cannot be ignored in the analysis of arrays which use this type of element.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A circular antenna utilizing phase only adaptive nulling
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A novel, phase-only adaptive nulling algorithm has been developed as an 'applique' for a multimode circular antenna. It provides the capability to suppress undesired jamming signals by spatial filtering. The algorithm minimizes the antenna's output power while maintaining the direction of its main beam. It has been verified through computer simulation and experimentation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Rectangular waveguide loaded by a radiating slot
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The design of phased arrays using open-ended waveguides requires the solution of singular integrodifferential equations, and the coupling between the higher modes of the guides leads to the blindness phenomenon. It is suggested that an array of rectangular waveguides loaded by radiating slots might be free of those problems. A rectangular guide loaded by a narrow slot is considered. The dominant-mode reflected wave and the fields of the evanescent modes generated by the magnetic current equivalent to the slot are obtained from explicit expressions previously reported. The measured and calculated values of the input resistance and reactance are plotted, showing fair agreement between theory and experiment. It is shown that the operational bandwidth of this radiator can be increased by a reactive stub.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Emulsions as materials with adjustable dielectric properties
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Emulsions are examined as materials with adjustable electrical properties (relative permittivity and conductivity). The emulsions are simple mixtures of oil, saline solution, and a stabilizing agent (emulsifier). The relative permittivity of oil is around two, while that of water is around 80. Thus, a wide range of relative permittivity can be obtained by mixing these components. The conductivity of the emulsion can be adjusted by changing the concentration of the electrolyte, sodium chloride, in the aqueous phase. Bruggeman's theoretical formula for the electrical constitutive parameters of a heterogeneous system is applied to the emulsions. A series of oil-in-water emulsions has been formulated for use in scale models; this involves the selection of an appropriate emulsifier. The electrical constitutive parameters of these emulsions are predicted by the simplified Bruggeman's formula for a wide range of volume fraction of oil and normality of the saline solution.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Near field testing on ACTS breadboard multibeam antenna (MBA)
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The NASA Advanced Communications Technology Satellite (ACTS) is discussed. To ensure successful development of the flight ACTS MBA, a breadboard model was fabricated and tested at a near-field range facility. The authors summarize the test results and their implications for a flight MBA design and development. The near-field testing activities validated the design tools (both analytical and manufacturing) used on the ACTS MBA, helped develop the flight MBA alignment procedure, assessed the wire-gridded subreflector performance and its RF effects, and provided engineering data to substantiate the flight MBA performance. The activities also demonstrated the near-field range's capability as an integration and test facility, compared to a testing-only facility offered by the traditional far-field range. This is particularly useful when developing a complicated antenna system such as ACTS MBA.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A linearly-polarized radial line slot antenna
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The authors present the design of a linearly polarized RLSA (radial line slot antenna). A key feature consists of the slot arrangement that realizes the linear polarization of the rotationally symmetric travelling wave excitation. The design is verified by experiments. Fresnel patterns indicate the reasonable XPD of more than 17 dB. To suppress the reflection from slots, beam tilting techniques should be used in the practical design of the linearly polarized RLSA.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Factors influencing sidelobes on copol patterns of centre fed dual reflector earth station antennas
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Various factors which have on influence in increasing the sidelobe levels in symmetrical Cassegrain antennas are highlighted. Also shown are computed and measured values of copol patterns for a 40-ft. Cassegrain antenna. A geometric optic synthesis method was adapted to shape the profile of this dual-reflector system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: What do you mean by a solution to an operator equation (electromagnetic problems)
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: It is demonstrated that even the simplest integral equation in electromagnetics does not provide a numerically stable solution. The instability is not in the computation process but with the operator itself. Hence, when dealing with an ill-posed operator, the comparison of various entities such as error in the solution or in the residuals, for such problems has to be performed subjectively and not objectively. This makes code validation a rather difficult problem as there is no fixed guide to get the datum for an arbitrary problem.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design of an array of printed-dipoles proximity-coupled to a perpendicular microstripline
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: An eight-element series-fed array was built with a 27 dB Chebyshev amplitude distribution in a standing wave configuration for broadside radiation. The amplitude distribution was controlled by adjusting the offsets, and the interelement spacing was decided by the propagation constant of the covered microstripline. The characteristic impedance and the equivalent element resonant resistances were used for impedance matching to a 50 Omega source. The measured and calculated radiation patterns are presented and found to be in good agreement.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Aperture coupled half-open cavity slot wide band antenna
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A discussion is presented of research which involves a novel aperture-coupled, wideband cavity-backed slot (CBS) antenna. The purpose is to seek an approach which could not only give a simple and economical design but also a better operating bandwidth. It was found that the aperture-coupled half-open cavity slot antenna can solve this problem. A description is given of the development and design of this CBS, and the experimental results for antenna patterns and impedance are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Adaptive beam-space nulling of multipath signals
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A beam-space nulling algorithm is described which has potential for applications in communication circuits which are degraded by multipath signals. Results are presented from tests of the algorithm using real multipath data. The data used in these tests were recorded using a beacon and a large aperture antenna. These measurements were carried out on an over-water path. The direct signal, i.e. the signal that propagated via the shortest path from the beacon to the antenna, is selected as the desired signal and the indirect signal(s), i.e. the signals that propagated via reflection from the surface of the water, as the unwanted signal(s). In many cases the wanted and unwanted signals are separated by less than a beamwidth. Two examples are given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A hybrid method for the calculation of transient EM scattering
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Analytical and numerical studies have made clear that singularity expansion methods (SEMs) for scattering responses are inadequate in early scattering time. However, it is efficient to use SEM in later scattering time, especially after creeping waves reach the observation point. A combination of a discrete Fourier transformation (DFT-SEM) and an SEM expansion is reported that gives good results in the entire time domain. The method avoids the difficulties of SEM in calculation of early time responses and is more efficient and exact than the DFT method alone. Because contributions to the response are considered over all the frequency domain, there is no restriction on the excitation, it can be an impulse that has a white spectrum. The solutions given by the DFT-SEM method have high precision and are insensitive to frequency-response errors.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Broad wall tilted slots on rectangular waveguides
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A broad wall slot with an offset from the center line and a tilt with respect to the axis, called a compound slot, has found applications in missile systems. The analysis of compound slots is rather involved, and, hence the design of compound slot arrays in the past relied on experimentally measured data. The author analyzes a compound slot radiating element and presents some numerical results. The normalized resonant length, backward and forward scattered TE/sub 10/ mode amplitude (b/sub 10/, c/sub 10/), and phase are shown for the case in which all the elements have an offset of 0.15" from the center line of the waveguide. Also shown are the complex coefficients of the expansion modes for the aperture magnetic currents.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Optimal source distributions for producing power maxima in lossy slabs and cylinders (microwave hyperthermia)
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Electromagnetic power deposition patterns in lossy simplified biological tissue models as a function of frequency are presented, along with a focusing method that constrains surface power. The size limitations and source distributions for heating with high spatial resolution patterns are derived. Using conductivity and permeability data for muscle tissue as a function of frequency, in conjunction with near-field focusing, the surface phase and amplitude functions that give the best power deposition patterns can be derived. The data establish the ideal capabilities for deep microwave hyperthermia as a cancer treatment modality.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Reflector antennas with suppressed sidelobes
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The radiation characteristics of a class of two-dimensional reflector antennas is investigated. An array of radiators is used to control the aperture field distribution and hence the gain and the sidelobe levels of the far radiated fields. The method of moments is used to find the induced surface current distribution, the aperture field, and the far-field pattern. Since the problem is two-dimensional, all radiators are considered to be line sources. The numerical results show that the gain is increased and the sidelobe levels are greatly reduced for strip, corner, circular, and parabolic reflector antennas by using three line sources with proper choice of their positions, amplitudes, and phase.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Frequency-selective reflectors using periodic dielectric layers
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The authors examine the feasibility of using periodically varying dielectric layers for implementing subreflectors that permit feed separation in large-aperture reflecting antenna systems. The specific periodic layers investigated are in the canonic form; they consist of alternating stripes in the form of rectangular bars having different dielectric constants. To illustrate their frequency-selection mechanism, the authors consider the simple case of a (TE) plane wave polarized along the y direction and incident at an angle theta in the xz plane perpendicular to the strips. The results reveal that the layer exhibits the desired frequency-selective properties, namely, total reflection at one frequency and total transmission at other well-separated frequencies. The approximate locations of the reflection and transmission bands can be predicted from the properties of an equivalent layer having a uniform dielectric constant equal to the average of that in the periodic layer.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A one-dimensional demonstration of the finite difference time domain technique using a personal computer
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The finite-difference time-domain technique for solving Maxwell's equation is considered. Referring to K.S. Yee's paper (1966), it is quite straightforward to reduce the finite-difference equations presented there to a one-dimensional geometry. This reduction still allows full control of the constitutive parameters at each cell, so that the result is the capability to analyze propagation through a planar stratified medium for normal incidence. Since the problem space is limited to one dimension, problem geometries involving, for example, reflection and transmission for a stratified slab several wavelengths thick may be computed with a simple Fortran program using a PC/AT or compatible computer with a coprocessor chip in just a few seconds. The one-dimensional formulation does allow specification of permittivity, permeability, and conductivity independently for each layer (cell), so the PC computations can be used to illustrate propagation through and reflection from lossy media. Furthermore, the constitutive parameters can be changed gradually to model the effects of tapering.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Aperture mutual coupling in a semi-infinite slotted array
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Quadrature integration and series summation of the periodic Green's function are used to efficiently compute the mutual admittance matrix for a planar phased array of thin slots with assumed cosinusoidal aperture electric field. The array is of infinite extent in the E-plane and is of finite extent in the H-plane. The H-plane excitation is arbitrary and the array is phase scanned in the E-plane. Resultant active aperture admittances and H-plane aperture distributions are calculated for uniform and 50 dB Chebyshev H-plane excitations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design of cross-polarization suppressed waveguide array for desired radiation pattern
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A general synthesis method is discussed for the realization of any desired radiation pattern using either an array of waveguide radiators excited through slot-coupled junctions, or an array of slots radiating into free space. An example is presented for realizing the amplitude distribution obtained by following T.T. Taylor's (1955) method of synthesis for a 28-dB sidelobe level for a five-element array.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Numerical analysis of conducting plate antenna near a plane reflector
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The authors develop a hybrid MM/UTD technique for treating arbitrarily shaped conducting plate antenna near a plane reflector. Numerical results of input admittances and far-field patterns are presented for antennas backed by a rectangular reflector. As examples, the authors consider a rectangular conducting plate monopole excited by a coaxial line in a distance d from the edge of a half infinite ground plane. As a second example, a pear-shaped conducting plate monopole excited at the centre of a square plate (36*36 cm/sup 2/) from a coaxial line (b=17.5 mm, a=7.6 mm) is investigated. The radiation pattern of conducting plate dipole backed by a square reflector is also shown. A delta source is used in the calculation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The adaptive nulling systems for a narrowband signal with a look-direction constraint
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: The problem of adaptively adjusting the weights of an array to eliminate unwanted interference sources (jammers) with an arbitrary look-direction constraint is considered. The technique uses the conjugate gradient method to eliminate the jammer components, thus, minimizing the error between the received signal and the actual one. This iterative method minimizes the L/sub 2/ norm, or the mean square error, and converges in a finite number of steps.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Dynamic field plots of single and coupled microstrip lines
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Dynamic field plots are provided for single and coupled strip structures over isotropic dielectric layers. A simple method based on the transmission matrix in the Fourier domain is used to generate the plots at different frequencies. Even and odd modes are generated. The dispersion effect for different modes is apparent at higher frequencies.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A small probe antenna for the self-check of a receiver in a monopulse planar array
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: A self-check of the sum and difference channels of a monopulse receiver can be realized using a small probe antenna placed at the proper position in the monopulse planar array. This results in a convenient operation because the planar array might not point at the aligning tower when self-checking. An example calculation is given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Wave scattering from finite metal strip gratings
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Numerical methods for the problem of scattering from periodic metal gratings has mostly been limited to the case of infinite extent. To solve the finite problem, the authors have proposed a microwave equivalent network approach that connects a finite number of locally homogeneous building blocks of a structure in tandem. To overcome the problem of introducing a radiation wave with a continuous spectrum into an equivalent network expressed only by the discrete terminal ports, the authors recompose the continuous radiation wave into a discrete set of so-called spectral composite modes by applying a complete set of orthonormal function in the spectral domain. As a result, they know the mode amplitude of all of the ports at the input terminal plane, if the incident wave illuminating a structure is expanded into spectral composite modes, providing completely the wave behavior along the structure. An analysis is presented for metal grating of zero thickness (t=0) illuminated by Gaussian beam waves incident in phase from both upper and lower sides with a slant angle of 15 degrees .<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An excitation matching approach to monopulse linear array synthesis with a sub-arrayed element feed network
publicationTitle: 1988 IEEE AP-S. International Symposium, Antennas and Propagation
abstract: Use of the two-module feed network for the monopulse linear array places restrictions on the performance of the monopulse array. This can be improved somewhat by utilizing subarraying to increase the number of degrees of freedom above that available with the two-module-network. A technique referred to as excitation matching is given for synthesizing an array with such a subarrayed feed network.
